# Psalm 138 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Of David. I give you thanks, O LORD, with my whole heart; before the gods I sing your praise;

**2** I bow down toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name for your steadfast love and your faithfulness, for you have exalted above all things your name and your word.

**3** On the day I called, you answered me; my strength of soul you increased.

**4** All the kings of the earth shall give you thanks, O LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth,

**5** and they shall sing of the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.

**6** For though the LORD is high, he regards the lowly, but the haughty he knows from afar.

**7** Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you preserve my life; you stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and your right hand delivers me.

**8** The LORD will fulfill his purpose for me; your steadfast love, O LORD, endures forever. Do not forsake the work of your hands.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 138.

- **138:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **138:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **138:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **138:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **138:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **138:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **138:2**: 'You-have-magnified above all your-name your-saying' — God's word is elevated even above his reputation; what he has spoken surpasses everything.
- **138:6**: 'The-lowly he-sees, and-the-haughty from-afar he-knows' — God's attention goes to the humble; the proud he perceives but keeps at distance.

### LOGOS
- **138:8**: 'The LORD will fulfill his purpose for me' — one of the strongest statements of divine providence in the Psalms. God completes what he begins.

### PNEUMA
- **138:6**: God pays close attention to the humble but only watches the proud from far away. Humility draws God near; pride keeps him at a distance. That's the divine operating system.
- **138:8**: 'The LORD will finish what he started in my life.' That's the promise: God doesn't start projects and abandon them. If he's working in you, he'll complete it.

— SOPHIA
